cues.en: After Hurricane Sandy in 2012, election officials in some parts of America decided that they would allow emergency electronic voting from home. You would download a ballot paper, fill it out, and then email or fax it back to them. And yes, some people still fax. This was a terrible idea, and here's why.
cues.zh: 2012年飓风桑迪过后，美国部分地区的选举官员决定允许在家进行紧急电子投票。你可以下载选票，填好后再通过电子邮件或传真发回给他们。是的，现在还有人发传真。这主意糟透了，原因如下。

cues.en: Physical voting is centuries old. In that time, pretty much every conceivable method of fraud has been tried, and has since been defended against. Because of that, attacks on physical voting don't scale well. It takes so much effort, so many people, and it only takes one person to leak your conspiracy, and the whole thing falls apart. But electronic voting? You can attack with one person. And it can take about the same effort to change one vote as it does to change a million, and it can be done without even setting foot in the country whose elections you're trying to rig. There are...
cues.zh: 实体投票已经存在了好几个世纪。在那段时间里，几乎所有能想到的作弊手段都被人试过，随后也都被防范了。因此，针对实体投票的攻击很难形成规模。这需要耗费巨大的精力，动用大量的人手，而且只要有一个人泄露密谋，全盘就都泡汤了。但电子投票呢？一个人就能发起攻击。改一张票和改一百万张票所花的力气可能差不多，甚至不用踏入你想操纵选举的那个国家一步就能搞定。选举有……

cues.en: two key parts of an election. First, anonymity. You cannot let anyone pay or bribe in order to change someone's vote or threaten them. If you put any identifying mark on your paper ballot, if you sign it, put your name on it, put a number on anything that could, in theory, be used to check how you voted, then your vote is thrown out.
cues.zh: 两个核心要素。首先是匿名性。你不能让任何人通过收买、贿赂或威胁来改变别人的投票。如果你在纸质选票上留下任何可识别的标记，比如签名、写上名字，或者写下任何理论上能用来查出你投给谁的数字，那你的选票就会作废。

cues.en: just so no one can be forced or bribed to vote a certain way. And yet, because you marked your vote and you put it into a sealed box, that box was only unsealed when it was surrounded by everyone with a stake in the election, you know that your vote has still been counted. Even though you will never see it again. That's the other key. Trust, or a complete lack of it. You never, ever, ever trust any one individual.
cues.zh: 这纯粹是为了防止有人被迫或被收买去按某种方式投票。然而，因为你划好了选票并投进密封箱里，而且那个箱子只有在所有利益相关方都在场监督时才会开封，所以你知道你的选票依然被计入了。哪怕你再也见不到它了。这就是另一个核心：信任，或者说是彻底的不信任。你绝不、绝不、绝不能信任任何一个个体。

cues.en: Ideally, you don't trust any two or three. People can be bribed, can be threatened, can be incompetent. I mean, hell, people have been all three of those things at the same time, but, like I said, the more physical votes you want to change, the more people it takes, and the less possible your attack gets. Everyone can see what's happening, and they can keep an eye on each other. Particularly if they don't trust the, uh, the despicable people on the other side. So, let's talk about voting machines. Problem number one!
cues.zh: 理想情况下，你连两三个人都不能信。人可能会被收买，可能会被威胁，也可能会办事不力。我是说，天哪，有些人这三样能全占了，但正如我所说，你想改动的实体选票越多，需要的人手就越多，攻击成功的可能性就越小。所有人都能看到正在发生什么，大家可以互相监督。尤其是当他们不信任……呃，不信任对立阵营那些讨厌的家伙时。那么，我们来谈谈投票机吧。第一个问题！

cues.en: Auditing the software and hardware. Because in theory you could have open source software that everyone has checked and everyone is happy with and that's been used for years. In theory. Never mind that you only actually do a full-scale test of this software every few years when there's actually an election. Let's say theoretically it can be done. How do you make sure that that software is what's actually loaded
cues.zh: 审查软件和硬件。因为理论上你可以使用开源软件，每个人都检查过且都满意，并且已经使用了好多年。理论上是这样。先不说你其实每隔几年大选时，才会真正对这套软件进行一次全面测试。假设理论上行得通，你又怎么保证那套软件就是实际加载到

cues.en: on that voting machine in front of you on the day of the election. And I know that immediately someone is going to want to comment about checksums or crypto, which is great, except now you have to trust the software that's checking that hash, or more likely, the one person who is checking it for you. You have just moved the problem. And if you're thinking, right now, ah, it's fine, I could verify that, then turn your brain the other way.
cues.zh: 选举当天摆在你面前的那台投票机上的软件呢？我知道马上就会有人想提校验和或加密算法，这很好，但问题是你现在必须信任检查那个哈希值的软件，或者更有可能的是，信任那个替你做检查的人。你只是把问题转移了而已。如果你此刻在想：啊，没关系，我能验证它，那就把思路反过来想想。

cues.en: and think, how could I break that? Because there are trillions of dollars. It's not an exaggeration. Trillions riding on the result of big elections. And that is an incredible motivation. If you're coming up with sneaky ways to get around it, believe me, so are lots of other people. Now, it might be one angry techie, but it might be an entire political party, or the huge corporations who want one party to win, or entire nation-states who want one party to win. And all that!
cues.zh: 然后想想，我怎么能攻破它？因为这里面有数万亿美元。不是夸张。数万亿美元都押在大型选举的结果上。这是极其强大的动机。如果你在想一些狡猾的办法绕过它，相信我，很多其他人也在想。现在，这可能是一个愤怒的技术人员，但也可能是一整个政党，或者希望某个政党获胜的巨型企业，或者希望某个政党获胜的整个民族国家。所有这些都可能！

cues.en: is assuming that you are even allowed to verify the software that's running, which you never are, because plugging unknown USB sticks into a voting machine is a bad idea. Not that that stops people plugging unknown USB sticks into a voting machine. It has literally happened. Let's remember, these machines have to be left in a room with the voter and no one else in order for the voter to cast their vote anonymously. Oh, and by the way, the machines are frequently programmed by sticking a USB into each of them in turn, so if you compromise the first one, jackpot!
cues.zh: 还得假设你甚至被允许验证正在运行的软件——而你从来不被允许，因为把未知 USB 盘插进投票机是个坏主意。但这并不能阻止人们把未知 USB 盘插进投票机。这事儿真的发生过。记住，为了让选民匿名投票，这些机器必须和选民单独留在一个房间里。哦，顺便说一句，这些机器经常是通过依次给每台插 USB 盘来编程的，所以如果你攻破了第一台，那就中大奖了！

cues.en: In practice, you don't have open source software, you have proprietary, un-audited software, which you just have to trust. This is real, by the way, around the world. There are some elections that run on this. And remember what I said? This is an election. You don't trust. And maybe you're thinking, okay, you can have an audit trail, you can have a paper backup that the machine prints out as you vote, in which case, congratulations, you have just invented the world's most expensive pencil. One of the reasons Britain gives people pencils for voting, by the way, is because we're worried that pens might be switched.
cues.zh: 实际上，你拿到的不是开源软件，而是专有的、未经审计的软件，你只能信任它。顺便说，这在世界各地都是真实存在的。有些选举就靠它运行。还记得我说过的吗？这是选举。你不能靠信任。也许你在想，好吧，可以有审计轨迹，可以让机器在你投票时打印纸质备份，那么恭喜你，你刚发明了世界上最贵的铅笔。顺便说，英国给人们铅笔投票的原因之一，就是我们担心笔会被调包。

cues.en: by any voter to contain disappearing ink. It might be an urban legend, sure. But if you want to do something like that, then erasing pencils way more difficult than just putting disappearing ink in there might be an urban legend, might be a plausible attack vector. That's the level of paranoia we're working out here. And if you think that you can get away with all this by using a pile of paper ballots and just counting them electronically,
cues.zh: 被任何选民换成含有消失墨水的笔。当然，这可能是都市传说。但如果你想做那种事，那么擦除铅笔比在里面放消失墨水要困难得多，这可能是个都市传说，也可能是个合理的攻击途径。这就是我们在这里讨论的偏执程度。如果你以为用一堆纸质选票并只用电子方式计票就能躲过这一切，

cues.en: An electronic counting machine is still a black box that a pile of ballots goes into and a mysterious number comes out of. They've got exactly the same problems. Problem number two. Votes in transit. There are three ways of moving the magic electronic ballot numbers from the voting machines to the final count. You could treat the machine like a regular ballot box, seal it in a plastic bag, move the physical machine with two people inside the vehicle to the count, and then you unseal it there. No one does this. You could...
cues.zh: 电子计票机仍然是个黑箱：一堆选票进去，一个神秘数字出来。它们有完全相同的问题。问题二。传输中的选票。把神奇的电子选票数字从投票机送到最终计票处有三种方式。你可以把机器当成普通投票箱，装进塑料袋封好，车内两人押运这台实体机器到计票处，然后在那里拆封。没人这么做。你可以……

cues.en: copy the result onto a handy USB stick and move the USB stick instead. Do I need to run through how easily? No, okay, obviously I don't. Or, and this is what usually happens, you could tell the voting machine to upload the results over the internet, optionally through a third-party central server, probably not over a secure connection, and probably without any checksums or tests. Problem number three!
cues.zh: 把结果拷到随手拿的U盘上，然后直接带走U盘。需要我细说这有多容易吗？不用，好吧，显然不用。或者——通常也是这么干的——你可以让投票机通过互联网上传结果，可能还要经过第三方的中央服务器，大概率没有走安全连接，而且大概率也没有任何校验和或测试。第三个问题来了！

cues.en: the central count program. Right at the end, there is the program that takes all these numbers, all these votes, and produces a final count. So now you have all the same problems that you have with the individual voting machines, except now only a few people can even see that computer, and it's been hidden away in a private warehouse somewhere for the last few years. So, you know, good luck verifying that. And all this, all this, is before we even talk about online voting.
cues.zh: 那就是中央计票程序。在流程的最末端，有一个程序会收集所有这些数字、所有这些选票，并生成最终结果。所以，单个投票机有的问题它全都有，而且现在只有极少数人能见到那台电脑，过去几年它还一直被藏在某个私人仓库里。所以，祝你好运去核验它吧。而所有这一切，所有这一切，都还没涉及到网络投票呢。

cues.en: You could talk about all the ways, you could hijack ballots, you could compromise computers, you could block an email address, because after Hurricane Sandy, the ballots were sent by email. Any of the ways, you could do a man in the middle attack on any of that. All possible. All entirely possible. And those are just fits a well designed system.
cues.zh: 你可以列举出所有手段：你可以劫持选票，可以黑进电脑，可以封锁某个邮箱地址——因为在“桑迪”飓风之后，选票就是用电子邮件发送的。你可以用任何手段对其中任何一环发起中间人攻击。全都做得到，完全有可能发生。而这还仅仅是针对设计良好的系统而言。

cues.en: There are reports of actual live elections, whether across-site scripting attacks in the e-voting page, where they misspelled one party's name, where they put the wrong party's logo next to a candidate. So, did I say elections? I meant election. That was all the same election, and it was one of the trials in Hampshire in 2007. But never mind all that!
cues.zh: 有实际公开选举的报道指出，电子投票页面出现了跨站脚本攻击，某个政党的名字被拼错了，候选人旁边还放错了党徽。等等，我说的是“多场选举”吗？我指的是“一场选举”。这些全都发生在同一次选举中，也就是2007年 Hampshire 的一次试点。不过先别管这些了！

cues.en: Depending on which security company you believe, somewhere between 5% and 50% of desktop computers around the world are infected with something. That's just the scammers trying to set up botnets and minor extortions on private computers. If you want to affect a load of votes, try infecting the computers at the public library. But never mind that!
cues.zh: 取决于你相信哪家安全公司的说法，全球有 5% 到 50% 的台式电脑都感染了某种恶意程序。这还只是骗子们为了在私人电脑上组建僵尸网络和搞点小敲诈而已。如果你想影响大批选票，不妨去黑掉公共图书馆的电脑。但先别管这个了！

cues.en: Because we've seen what some big scary countries and big scary corporations can do when they put their mind to it. Given that someone, someone, designed an immensely complicated worm that spread around the world just to break some Iranian centrifuges, imagine what someone could do if they wanted to throw an online election. Remember, when you hear, just trust us, or just trust me, or it's a computer it doesn't go wrong in an election, something has already gone disastrously wrong.
cues.zh: 因为我们已经见识过，某些可怕的大国和可怕的大企业一旦下定决心能做出什么。既然有人、有某些人曾设计过极其复杂的蠕虫病毒席卷全球，仅仅为了破坏伊朗的离心机，那你可以想象一下，如果有人想要操纵一场网络选举，他们能做出什么来。请记住，在选举中，一旦你听到“相信我们就好”，或者“相信我就行”，或者“这是电脑，它不会出错”，那就说明事情早就已经错得一塌糊涂了。

cues.en: Imagine all this electronic voting only without computers. Would you be happy walking up to someone anonymous in a ballot box? Or worse, just calling someone on your phone, telling them your vote, but they promise to keep it secret. And at the end of the election, all those people who've been sitting on their own phone up one other person in private and tell their results. And then that final person who promises to count it all up accurately just announces who's won. Because that is essentially what electronic voting is. It is a terrible idea. And if a government...
cues.zh: 想象一下，把所有这些电子投票拿掉电脑会怎样。如果让你走到投票箱前一个匿名的人面前，你愿意吗？或者更糟，直接给某个人打电话报出你的投票，对方承诺替你保密。在选举结束时，所有那些守在自己电话前的人，再私下打给另一个人汇报结果。最后那个人承诺会准确无误地统计全部数据，然后宣布谁赢了。因为电子投票本质上就是这么回事。这个主意烂透了。而如果一个政府……

cues.en: ever promises to use it, hope they don't manage it before you get a chance to vote them out. That's the problem with filming in a big city, mate. Because you can hear Rattley McRattleson and his massive tray of whatever it is is moving. Between that and the bagpiper and the sirens, we've filmed in front of a clock. There's going to be some pedant who is going to run through this and work out how many takes we've done and what order they were in, and how many times I had to repeat that bit where I got really flustered.
cues.zh: 不管是谁承诺要用它，希望他们别在你来得及投票把他们赶下台之前就得逞。伙计，这就是在大城市拍摄的麻烦。因为你能听到 Rattley McRattleson 和他那一大托盘不知道什么东西在动。再加上风笛手和警笛，我们是在一座钟前面拍的。肯定会有个爱抠细节的人把这段过一遍，算出我们拍了几条、顺序怎样，还有我那段特别慌的地方重来了多少遍。

cues.en: Yeah Never mind the fact that I started with slightly damp hair and I've ended with kind of Belinda Carlisle going on here
cues.zh: 是啊，别提我一开始头发还有点湿，拍到最后都有点 Belinda Carlisle 那味儿了。
